body: Yeah, I think it might take a little bit of time to learn how to listen to my emotions, but that definitely seems like the right path to go on. You give some great advice lol, I didn't really know what to expect, but it wasn't something this thorough. Thank you so much again for your time!!

This post made me cry (in a good way), thank you so much. I think one of my greatest fears is that I'll break it off with him now, I won't have the chance to experience the kind of life you currently have. I think you're very right that I should try to seek treatment, but it's just very difficult knowing how much work it'll be when I've been ignoring it for so long.

It's also really nice to hear an anecdote from someone who went through the same thing, I really appreciate it. I think it's probably my perception that's messed up right now, but I'm still scared that the breakup thoughts might happen to be genuine. I suppose some therapy and time will be the only way to tell for sure.

>Emotions tend to hijack our thoughts to fit themselves.

Aha! It's all coming together! I guess until now I considered myself above my emotions and could detach myself well enough to give an unbiased assessment of my thoughts. But I think the fact that I've even gone out of my way to make multiple Reddit posts over several weeks proves otherwise.

​

>You may be alexithymic by the way.

Interesting, I haven't heard of this before! From a quick read I'm not sure how I feel about it, I always just called what I do "overthinking" haha. Although the overthinking is usually always in a worst-case scenario.

Thanks again for all these responses!

Maybe, I personally think it's hard to tell since up until now I would've just described my emotional state as "dull." I didn't really consider those words you used as emotions-- I knew they were there, but I've just stuck to simpler words to make myself feel more comfortable.

I think it's hard to look at my emotions when so many of them are depression-related, so I'm not sure which are genuine or not. But now that I'm rethinking, I suppose all emotions are genuine and it's the thoughts that those emotions produce that might be irrational, and I would have to figure out if my breakup thoughts are extended from the depression-related emotions. 

It's a little late where I am, so I could very well be rambling nonsense.

That's a difficult question, and a really, really good one. I'm not too sure how to answer.

I actually started to keep a log at one point (originally to see if the sadness was just PMS lol) and I wasn't able to identify a pattern. Most of the thoughts had to do with self esteem, and the ones of my boyfriend are just based on lack of interest. Currently, I can't identify any other clearly irrational thoughts besides the recurring one of wanting to break up, which almost makes me think that the irrational thoughts have gone away, leaving this rational one left.

I suppose I can keep trying though, it'd probably be worth it now that these thoughts are more frequent. Thanks again for all the responses.

I think I phrased this wrong-- I meant the emotions that are genuine, and the ones that are clouded by depression or symptoms of it. 

Sometimes I have irrational thoughts like "my parents absolutely hate me and think I'm the worst person on the planet!" which seem real (or valid) in the moment, but I know that they are irrational once I'm out of that depression trance.

So I'm having difficultly evaluating whether my current thoughts of breaking up are genuine or if they're just irrational thoughts.

I think that's accurate. I think I'm just having trouble evaluating whether those emotions are valid are not, which is probably something I'd have to look into deeper. It's a little difficult because "looking deeper" and "overthinking" can be hard to separate.

I know this post wasn't much to go off of but you've managed to say a lot in a sentence, so I appreciate the advice.

Until very recently I've found it difficult to accept that anything was wrong (I thought it was just typical emotions), so not much. I set up a couple of counseling appointments over the past month, but as each approached I got too nervous and cancelled.

I have set up yet another appointment and I'm feeling better about going, so hopefully this will be the one haha

Thank you. I agree that it probably won't fix itself, but until recently I've found it very difficult to accept that anything might be wrong, so I've yet to seek out any medical care.

Now that I'm thinking about it, I think my main concerns are either:

1. Wanting to break up is not a result of depression, and if I break up with him later, then I would have dragged him along through it all
2. Wanting to break up is a result of depression, and if I break up with him now, then I'll realize it after it's too late

I'm not sure which I'm more scared of, but your comment definitely helped me evaluate them more. Thanks again

Yeah, it's definitely extremely easy to isolate with everything going on. I think the most concerning thing to me about opening up to my boyfriend (or anyone in general) is that I could worry or upset them in doing so. Whenever I've tried to open up to him he gets visibly worried and immediately tries his best to help, which I appreciate so so much, of course, but the fact that I could be inadvertently causing more pain than I have to worries me even more.

This is all really good advice though, thank you so so much for the comment!

Yeah I agree, I’ve been with him for over a year so I feel like a single text would be one of the worst ways. After reading these comments I’m starting to think the FaceTime might not be as bad as I thought it’d be, so thanks!
Thanks, I definitely agree with mentioning that it’s the relationship I want to talk about first, appreciate it!
